Q: Getting All hosts are taken by other resources with Nginx Ingress Controller A:

Please keep in mind that there are 3 types of Nginx: Open Source Nginx Ingress Controller, Nginx Incorporated (nginx inc), and Nginx Incorporated Plus.

As I mentioned in the comments, the issue was caused by resources using the same host. It's called Host Collisions.

A host collision occurs when multiple resources configure the same host. The Ingress Controller supports two options for handling host collisions:

  • Choosing the Winner

If multiple resources contend for the same host, the Ingress Controller will pick the winner based on the creationTimestamp of the resources: the oldest resource will win. In case there is more than one oldest resource (their creationTimestamp is the same), the Ingress Controller will choose the resource with the lexicographically smallest uid.

  • Merging Configuration for the Same Host

It is possible to merge the configuration for multiple Ingress resources for the same host. One common use case for this approach is distributing resources across multiple namespaces.

OP confirmed that this was solved by changes made in another Ingress resource in another namespace.

I was able to resolve this. There was one more Ingress in another namespace

Q: Why use "where 1=2" on a SQL CREATE TABLE syntax? A:

In SQL Server

select * into table1 from table2 where 1=2 (Only Structure)

select * into table1 from table2 where 1=1 (Structure with data)

Q: Create table (structure) from existing table A:

Try:

Select * Into <DestinationTableName> From <SourceTableName> Where 1 = 2

Note that this will not copy data, indexes, keys, etc. To learn why Where 1 = 2 is included, see Why use "where 1=2" on a SQL CREATE TABLE syntax?

If you want to copy the entire structure, you need to generate a Create Script of the table. You can use that script to create a new table with the same structure. You can then also dump the data into the new table if you need to.

If you are using Enterprise Manager, just right-click the table and select copy to generate a Create Script.

Q: Extract passphrase from Jenkins' credentials.xml A: 
import com.cloudbees.plugins.credentials.*
import com.cloudbees.plugins.credentials.common.*
import com.cloudbees.plugins.credentials.domains.*
import com.cloudbees.plugins.credentials.impl.*
import com.cloudbees.jenkins.plugins.sshcredentials.impl.*
import org.jenkinsci.plugins.plaincredentials.impl.*
import jenkins.model.Jenkins
import groovy.json.JsonOutput
import hudson.util.Secret

def systemStore = Jenkins.instance
    .getExtensionList('com.cloudbees.plugins.credentials.SystemCredentialsProvider')[0]
    ?.getStore()

def domain = Domain.global()
def result = []

if (systemStore) {
    systemStore.getCredentials(domain).each { cred ->

        def entry = [
            scope      : "system",
            id         : cred.id,
            type       : cred.class.simpleName,
            description: cred.description
        ]

        switch (cred) {

            case UsernamePasswordCredentialsImpl:
                entry.username = cred.username
                entry.password_encrypted =
                    cred.password?.getEncryptedValue()
                entry.decrypt = hudson.util.Secret.decrypt(entry.password_encrypted)
                break

            case StringCredentialsImpl:
                entry.secret_encrypted =
                    cred.secret?.getEncryptedValue()
                entry.decrypt = hudson.util.Secret.decrypt(entry.secret_encrypted)
                break

            case FileCredentialsImpl:
                entry.filename = cred.fileName
                entry.content_encrypted =
                    cred.secretBytes?.getEncryptedValue()
                entry.decrypt = hudson.util.Secret.decrypt(entry.content_encrypted)
                break

            case BasicSSHUserPrivateKey:
                entry.username = cred.username
                entry.privateKey_encrypted =
                    Secret.fromString(cred.privateKey).getEncryptedValue()
                entry.decrypt = hudson.util.Secret.decrypt(entry.privateKey_encrypted)
                break

            case CertificateCredentialsImpl:
                entry.certificate_encrypted =
                    cred.keyStoreSource?.keyStore?.getEncryptedValue()
                entry.decrypt = hudson.util.Secret.decrypt(entry.certificate_encrypted)
                break
        }

        result << entry
    }
}

println JsonOutput.prettyPrint(JsonOutput.toJson(result))

Q: Picture's srcset and sizes seem to be fine, but PageSpeed loads a wrong image A:

I am experiencing the exact same issue, and it is very frustrating. In the mobile test, PageSpeed Insights explicitly reports a device viewport of 412 × 823 with a DPR of 1.75.

Based on this, an image with sizes="100vw" should have the browser select the closest available source that is equal to or larger than 412 × 1.75 ≈ 721 px.

I tested this extensively using PageSpeed Insights and even created a dedicated test page with an image using sizes="100vw" and a srcset defined in 5 px increments (e.g., 400, 405, 410, 415, etc.). In all cases, the browser correctly selected the closest match—725 px in this example. Yet PageSpeed Insights still reports an error:

“Improve image delivery — This image file is larger than it needs to be (725×725) for its displayed dimensions (412×412). Use responsive images to reduce the image download size.”

This indicates a disconnect within PageSpeed Insights: the browser emulator correctly accounts for DPR when selecting the image, but the test evaluator does not. As a result, the evaluator incorrectly expects the image to be smaller in the mobile test.

Importantly, this issue affects only the Lab data in PageSpeed Insights. The real-user data (CrUX) correctly reflects the DPR-aware behavior.

There's currently an Issue about this on Github: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/issues/16579

Q: Docker with amazonlinux A:

I had the same goal of testing instances in development environment and initially I thought it should be as easy as docker run amazonlinux:2 -it. But I was so wrong and it took me almost one full day to get it to work!

Funny thing is when you google "amazonlinux Docker" it's often people trying to install "Docker in amazonlinux", but here we want to install "amazonlinux in Docker"!

We also want to install Docker in that amazonlinux, so basically "Docker in amazonlinux in Docker" which is "Docker in Docker" eventually! ;D*

My findings:

  • Amazonlinux in Docker (created via FROM amazonlinux:2) is so bare and empty that it doesn't even have basic stuffs like sudo or passwd.) New AWS EC2 instances do.
  • In order to have your serviced properly working (to start any daemon, including Docker Daemon), you need to have /usr/sbin/init be there (via yum install initscripts and actually called. However, the meat you want to play with need your shell to start from /bin/bash.
  • You are running a Docker within a Docker. That needs to be priviledged from the host in your docker run via --priviledged.
  • You need to share the /sys/fs/cgroup from your host machine (it can be read-only) for it to be able to properly initialize docker daemon.

My solution:

1) To fulfill the first two issues above, your Dockerfile can be:

FROM amazonlinux:2

RUN yum update -y && yum install -y initscripts;

CMD ["/usr/sbin/init"]

2) Build an image from it, e.g. docker build . -t ax1

3) Then, to address the latter two issues above, run a detached (running in background) container from it, priviledged, with a shared volume to your /sys/fs/cgroup. e.g.

docker run --name ac11 -d --privileged -v /sys/fs/cgroup:/sys/fs/cgroup:ro ax1

4) Finally you can bash into it using docker exec -it ac11 bash

5) Now, it's very close to a new EC2 instance. (Yet, missing sudo, actual ec2-user and other stuffs that we skipped in our Dockerfile to keep this solution simple.)

Anyway, now you can install docker as instructed by AWS Docs. That is, once you are in the container, do:

amazon-linux-extras install -y docker;

and then restart the docker service once:

service docker restart;

Now, docker ps should be working!
